text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The centre-left Social Democrats said the local polls were not wholly fair, therefore do not recognise the result and repeat their request for fresh general elections.
- U.S. citizens of Albanian origin support Bill Clinton for a second term as U.S. president as he voiced support for a re-run of Albania's last general elections.
- Tirana's new mayor Albert Brojka promised to increase the amount of green space in the capital.
- A 28-year old pregnant woman from northern Albania became the most recent victim of the country's polio outbreak.
- Leaders of the confederation of trade unions said their strike failed because it was not supported by the main trade union.
- The World Bank representative in Albania Carlos Elbirt says the high budget deficit remains the main problem for the government to resolve.
- Government urges the population to use kerosene and gas for heating to save electrical power.
- World War Two mines threaten to take more lives in Albania, an anti-mine committee said.
- A new highway to the south has taken up some 280,000 square meters from communities living in the Durres-Rrogozhine area, for which they are to be compensated in leks.
- Two members of parliament for the ethnic Greek Human Rights Union Party decided to take their seats in parliament after five months, Speaker Pjeter Arbnori said.
- Parliament will compile a new constitution by inviting more non-parliamentary parties and experts in the organising committee, Arbnori said.
- Italian authorities are fighting against Albanian smugglers of illegal emigrants and drugs in order to quell the strengthening of links with the Italian Mafia.
- A fire last Saturday at the Ballsh oil processing mill in southern Albania injured four workers.
- Most of the Albanian right- and left-wing politicians favour Bill Clinton for a second term as U.S. president. The government has made no comment.
